edges.description: The truncated, intrinsically disordered GS-domain polypeptide self-assembles into oligomers and amyloid fibrils.
The oligomeric (not fibrillar) form of mutant corneodesmosin is cytotoxic to keratinocytes.
Toxicity of mutant corneodesmosin to the follicle is the accepted explanation for the progressive hair loss, but no study follows it from oligomers to follicle loss in human scalp.
Failing scalp follicles produce sparse, fine hair from childhood.
Loss of scalp follicle output culminates in near-complete baldness.
edges.target: Near-Complete Scalp Baldness in Young Adulthood

edges.description: Failing scalp follicles produce fine, easily plucked hairs.

edges.limitations: A null allele rather than a truncated aggregating protein, with a lethal barrier defect that HSS patients do not have; follicle degeneration here follows epidermal barrier failure and desmosome breakage, not perifollicular amyloid.

evidence.reference_title: Hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp is associated with nonsense mutations in CDSN encoding corneodesmosin.
evidence.snippet: We have identified nonsense mutations in the gene CDSN (encoding corneodesmosin) in three families suffering from hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp (HSS; OMIM 146520).

evidence.reference_title: A non-sense mutation in the corneodesmosin gene in a Mexican family with hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp.
evidence.snippet: Our data provide molecular genetic evidence for a 3rd stop mutation in exon 2 of the CDSN gene being responsible for HSS.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the CDSN gene cause peeling skin disease and hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp.
evidence.snippet: Monoallelic mutations in CDSN have also been described in an autosomal dominant inherited genodermatosis: hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp.

nodes.description: A heterozygous premature stop codon in exon 2 of CDSN yields a truncated corneodesmosin that keeps the N-terminal glycine/serine-rich adhesive domain. The clustering of all known HSS stop codons in one short region, and the fact that biallelic null alleles cause a different disease, argue that the HSS allele acts through its abnormal product rather than through simple haploinsufficiency.

evidence.reference_title: A non-sense mutation in the corneodesmosin gene in a Mexican family with hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp.
evidence.snippet: All to date known nonsense mutations responsible 3 for HSS are clustered in a region of 40 amino acids which is in accordance with a dominant negative effect conferred by aggregates of truncated CDSN proteins.

evidence.reference_title: A new amyloidosis caused by fibrillar aggregates of mutated corneodesmosin.
evidence.snippet: Truncated mutants of CDSN ((mut)CDSN), which bear the N-terminal adhesive Gly/Ser-rich domain (GS domain) of the protein, abnormally accumulate as amorphous deposits at the periphery of hair follicles and in the papillary dermis of the patient skin.

genetic_context.description: NEOMORPHIC follows the amyloid work, which shows the truncated product forming toxic oligomers and fibrils, a property wild-type corneodesmosin does not have. An earlier family report read the clustered stop codons as a dominant-negative effect of the aggregates, but no study shows the mutant protein interfering with the wild-type protein. Either way the mechanism is dominant and is not haploinsufficiency.

molecular_functions: self-association of the corneodesmosin glycine/serine-rich domain

nodes.description: Remaining scalp hairs are fine, vellus-like and easily pulled out.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp with the combination of botanic extracts and minoxidil: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Dermatologic examination showed thinning and fine hair that were easily pulled out, no loss of eyebrows and eyelashes, no abnormalities in toenails and fingernails

nodes.description: Ring-shaped oligomers of mutant corneodesmosin are toxic to cultured keratinocytes, which is the proposed cellular basis for follicle damage. This has been shown in culture only; the follicular keratinocyte population that is affected in vivo has not been identified.

evidence.reference_title: A new amyloidosis caused by fibrillar aggregates of mutated corneodesmosin.
evidence.snippet: We showed that the ring-shaped oligomers of (mut)CDSN, but not the fibrillar forms, are toxic to cultured keratinocytes.

nodes.description: Epidermal ablation of Cdsn causes neonatal death from epidermal tearing; grafted knockout skin develops a barrier defect and then epidermal and hair-follicle degeneration. It models loss of corneodesmosin, which is the peeling-skin mechanism, not the truncated-protein amyloid of HSS.

evidence.reference_title: Corneodesmosin gene ablation induces lethal skin-barrier disruption and hair-follicle degeneration related to desmosome dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: The epidermis was first hyperproliferative with a thick cornified layer, then, both the epidermis and the hair follicles degenerated.

nodes.description: The progressive loss leads to complete or almost complete scalp baldness by the third decade. Severity varies, and some carriers retain thin scalp hair.

evidence.reference_title: Corneodesmosin gene ablation induces lethal skin-barrier disruption and hair-follicle degeneration related to desmosome dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: CDSN nonsense mutations are associated with hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp, a rare disease that leads to complete baldness in young adults.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the CDSN gene cause peeling skin disease and hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp.
evidence.snippet: However, the mother of the proband, also bearing this mutation, showed hypotrichosis but was not completely bald.

nodes.description: Scalp hair is normal or near-normal in infancy; diffuse thinning begins in childhood (often around 5-6 years) and progresses steadily. Hair is fine and easily pulled out. Eyebrows, eyelashes, body hair and nails are spared.

evidence.reference_title: A non-sense mutation in the corneodesmosin gene in a Mexican family with hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp.
evidence.snippet: The affected individuals experience a diffuse progressing hair loss from childhood to adulthood that is confined to the scalp.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp with the combination of botanic extracts and minoxidil: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Affected individuals have normal hair from birth to infancy, but hair loss begins at 5–6 years of age and continues to worsen to almost complete baldness by 20–30 years of age.

nodes.description: Scalp follicles that grew normal hair in infancy produce progressively thinner hair through childhood and fail by early adulthood, while follicles elsewhere are unaffected. Why the scalp alone is involved is not explained.

evidence.reference_title: Corneodesmosin gene ablation induces lethal skin-barrier disruption and hair-follicle degeneration related to desmosome dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: CDSN nonsense mutations are associated with hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp, a rare disease that leads to complete baldness in young adults.

evidence.reference_title: Corneodesmosin gene ablation induces lethal skin-barrier disruption and hair-follicle degeneration related to desmosome dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: The strong adhesive function that the protein confers on corneodesmosomes also seems necessary for maintaining the architecture of the hair follicle.

nodes.description: Gentamicin promotes ribosomal read-through of the CDSN premature stop codon and restored full-length corneodesmosin synthesis in patient keratinocytes. A 6-month pilot of topical gentamicin in four patients partially improved scalp hair. This is experimental, not established therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of hereditary hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp with topical gentamicin.
evidence.snippet: To validate the in vitro data, we conducted a pilot clinical trial where the scalp of four patients was treated topically with gentamicin for 6 months, demonstrating significant improvement as ascertained by the Severity of Alopecia Tool score.

nodes.description: The mutant corneodesmosin aggregates into ring-shaped oligomers and amyloid-like fibrils that bind Congo red and thioflavin T. In patient skin these accumulate as deposits at the periphery of hair follicles and in the papillary dermis, together with serum amyloid P component.

biological_processes: amyloid fibril formation by truncated corneodesmosin

evidence.reference_title: Hypotrichosis simplex of the scalp is associated with nonsense mutations in CDSN encoding corneodesmosin.
evidence.snippet: Truncated CDSN aggregates were detected in the superficial dermis and at the periphery of hair follicles.

evidence.reference_title: A new amyloidosis caused by fibrillar aggregates of mutated corneodesmosin.
evidence.snippet: Here, we present evidence that the (mut)CDSN deposits display an affinity for amyloidophilic dyes, namely Congo red and thioflavin T. We also detected the serum amyloid protein component in the dermis of HSS patients.

evidence.reference_title: A new amyloidosis caused by fibrillar aggregates of mutated corneodesmosin.
evidence.snippet: The amyloid-like nature of the fibrils was demonstrated by dye binding and Fourier transform infrared spectrometry measurements.
